sources.entry: X Twitter Scraper - Agent skill and MCP server for tweet search, user lookup, follower export, media download, webhooks, and confirmation-gated X actions. MIT.

summary.one_liner: A hosted X (Twitter) scraper API, MCP server, and agent Skill set from Xquik that searches tweets, looks up profiles, runs bulk extractions, and sends signed webhooks, billed per delivered result.
summary.what_it_does: The README documents a REST API at Xquik with a single x-api-key credential for searching tweets with server-side filters (language, minimum likes, excluding replies/retweets/quotes) and paging with next_cursor. It also covers profile lookups, follower and reply extraction, and bulk extraction jobs with estimates, result caps, and JSON/CSV/XLSX/PDF-style exports. Monitoring of accounts and keywords is offered with HMAC-signed webhooks and replayable events. The project ships as Agent Skills and a hosted MCP server for AI clients, plus TypeScript, Python, and other SDKs, a Go CLI, and an Apify Actor. Connected X account actions (posting, DMs, likes, follows) are available once an X account is linked, and the README says agents must never receive X passwords, cookies, or 2FA codes.
use_cases: search tweets by keyword with engagement filters
export follower or reply lists to CSV or JSON
monitor X accounts or keywords and receive webhooks
give an AI agent read access to X data via MCP
migrate app code away from the official X API
notable: Pay-per-delivered-result billing: 1 credit per returned tweet, estimates available before bulk jobs
Server-side tweet and profile filters applied before billing
Hosted MCP server exposing docs, search, and execute tools for AI clients
Signed webhooks with HMAC verification and event cursors for recovery after downtime
Official SDKs across many languages plus integrations with n8n, Zapier, Make, and Pipedream
caveats: Requires an Xquik account and API key; usage is metered in credits and pay-as-you-go pricing applies
Not affiliated with X Corp; deleted, protected, or restricted content may stay inaccessible and optional fields can be omitted
Active monitors cost 30 credits per hour each, and private reads or X actions need a connected X account
